1	\section*{Limitations}
2	\label{sec:limitations}
3	
4	\paragraph{Full-replacement vs.\ accumulation.}
5	All experiments use full-replacement recursive chains, where each depth fully replaces the prior training corpus. Real-world contamination typically involves accumulation, where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions across iterations \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate}. Under accumulation, depth signal should attenuate because each generation retains human-originated distributional properties. Our results therefore represent an upper bound on feature separability; extending the framework to accumulation settings, where depth becomes a continuous mixing parameter, is a priority for future work.
6	Segment-level estimation in mixed-depth documents remains open (Appendix~\ref{app:mixed_depth}), as our framework assumes uniform depth per passage.
7	
8	\paragraph{Controlled experimental setting.}
9	The primary benchmark uses Wikipedia seed text with controlled LoRA fine-tuning (1--1.5B models), a design that isolates the depth variable but diverges from wild contamination.
10	Domain bias controls confirm depth as the dominant factor: LOGO accuracy (72.1\%) matches standard CV (72.0\%), seed-group prediction is at chance (10.2\%; Appendix~\ref{app:domain_bias}).
11	Cross-scale experiments (7--14B, \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}) show signal that attenuates with scale; at 14B, d0/d1 separability nearly vanishes ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$) while d1--d3 discrimination persists; this constitutes a boundary condition for the current feature set (confounded by five factors; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_confounds}).
12	
13	\paragraph{Cross-strategy deployment constraint.}
14	Cross-strategy transfer induces a d1/d2 boundary inversion under temperature sampling.
15	Per-strategy z-score normalization partially corrects the inversion under logistic regression (GPT-2~XL d1v2 AUC $0.24{\to}0.56$, OLMo $0.19{\to}0.70$) but yields negligible improvement for the Random Forest ($\Delta < 0.02$\,pp); a two-stage pipeline is needed for reliable cross-strategy deployment.
16	In strategy-unknown settings, d1--d3 accuracy drops to 45.9\%; the pipeline recovers 11.5\,pp, though gains vary across models (GPT-2~XL $+$16.4\,pp vs.\ Pythia $+$8.0\,pp).
17	
18	\paragraph{d0 inflation of headline metrics.}
19	Depth~0 (human-written text) is near-perfectly separable (recall $>$97\%), inflating four-class accuracy.
20	Cross-model transfer of 66.4\% is substantially driven by d0; d2 recall drops to 26.8\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).
21	We report d1--d3 balanced accuracy alongside all four-class headlines to address this inflation.
22	
23	\paragraph{Domain-dependent false positive rate.}
24	On editorial text (WikiText-103), all classifiers achieve $\geq$98.5\% d0 accuracy, but on web-crawl data (C4, 5{,}000 passages), per-model FPR ranges from 4.7\% (OLMo) to 22.4\% (GPT-2~XL).
25	A pooled RF classifier evaluated on larger corpora (10{,}000 passages each) yields 34\% FPR on C4 and 17\% on FineWeb \cite{penedo2024_fineweb}; the gap reflects quality filtering in FineWeb removing feature-anomalous text that triggers false positives.
26	Misclassifications concentrate in template/SEO content with elevated repetition features (\texttt{rep\_3gram} $+$37\%, \texttt{rep\_4gram} $+$75\% vs.\ correctly classified d0).
27	Confidence thresholding ($P(\mathrm{d0}) \geq 0.15$) reduces pooled FPR from 34\%/17\% to 2.8\%/0.7\% on C4/FineWeb at minimal accuracy cost ($-$0.3\,pp); high FPR is therefore a decision-threshold problem, not a fundamental calibration defect, though the optimal threshold remains domain-dependent (Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}).
28	
29	\paragraph{Adversarial robustness.}
30	Adversarial paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase} could disrupt the perplexity tail features that drive classification; depth estimation's robustness under such attacks is untested.
31	
32	\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}
33	Our EDD definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically, as observed in all our configurations.
34	However, \citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).
35	Our cross-strategy transfer results provide an empirical example: training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature yields d1-vs-d2 AUC as low as 0.129 (GPT-2~XL) and 0.253 (OLMo), violating the monotonicity assumption.
36	In such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.
37	The choice of threshold $T$ is also application-dependent: at $T{=}0.80$, several cells lose one depth level relative to $T{=}0.75$.
38	
39	\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}
40	Reference model choice affects classification accuracy by up to 11\,pp; same-family references yield optimal performance, though all configurations exceed $2.5\times$ chance.
41	Surprisal-based features are computed relative to Pythia-1.4B, which coincides with one of the three generators.
42	For the Pythia pipeline this constitutes self-model feature extraction, while OLMo and GPT-2~XL measurements are cross-model.
43	The self-reference configuration yields a 4--11\,pp advantage over cross-model references (Table~\ref{tab:ref_ablation}); Pythia results in Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} ($^\dagger$) should be interpreted with this caveat.
44	An ablation with OLMo-1B and GPT-2 XL as alternative references shows accuracy ranging from 67--79\% across three reference architectures (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), all exceeding $2.5\times$ chance; same-family reference yields optimal performance ($\Delta{\leq}$11\,pp).
45	The choice of reference model affects feature values; a different reference model may shift absolute feature magnitudes and potentially alter discriminability at depth boundaries.
46	Reference-free surface features alone achieve 53.7\% (partial signal in lexical statistics) but trail the full pipeline by 25pp; surprisal-based features are therefore essential.
47	Simple multi-reference ensembling does not outperform the best single reference (73.7\% vs.\ 78.6\%).
48	
49	\paragraph{Single LoRA instance.}
50	Cross-seed replication covers 3 of 9 cells (Pythia, OLMo, GPT-2~XL nucleus); seed=43 yields $+$0.1 to $+$3.2\,pp higher accuracy, with 2/3 deltas statistically significant (non-overlapping CIs).
51	Feature rankings and depth ordering are consistent across seeds, but single-seed absolute accuracy carries ${\sim}$1--3\,pp uncertainty; cross-cell comparisons should be interpreted cautiously.
52	
53	\paragraph{Additional caveats.}
54	Depth signal scales with passage length (68.4\% at 128 tokens, 77.8\% at 512; Appendix~\ref{app:length_ablation}), saturating near 500 tokens.
55	Prompted generation was validated on only 1 of 9 cells (GPT-2~XL nucleus); generalization to other model--strategy configurations under prompted conditions is not established.
56	Detection features degrade under domain shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}, and curated synthetic data may not trigger collapse \cite{falahati2026_curated}, attenuating the fingerprints we exploit.
57	
58	\section*{Ethics Statement}
59	
60	This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
61	No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
62	Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
63	Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
64	This research used AI coding assistants for experiment implementation and writing drafts.
65	All scientific decisions, experimental design, and result interpretation were conducted by the authors.

\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\paragraph{Full-replacement vs.\ accumulation.}
All experiments use full-replacement recursive chains, where each depth fully replaces the prior training corpus. Real-world contamination typically involves accumulation, where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions across iterations \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate}. Under accumulation, depth signal should attenuate because each generation retains human-originated distributional properties. Our results therefore represent an upper bound on feature separability; extending the framework to accumulation settings, where depth becomes a continuous mixing parameter, is a priority for future work.
Segment-level estimation in mixed-depth documents remains open (Appendix~\ref{app:mixed_depth}), as our framework assumes uniform depth per passage.

\paragraph{Controlled experimental setting.}
The primary benchmark uses Wikipedia seed text with controlled LoRA fine-tuning (1--1.5B models), a design that isolates the depth variable but diverges from wild contamination.
Domain bias controls confirm depth as the dominant factor: LOGO accuracy (72.1\%) matches standard CV (72.0\%), seed-group prediction is at chance (10.2\%; Appendix~\ref{app:domain_bias}).
Cross-scale experiments (7--14B, \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}) show signal that attenuates with scale; at 14B, d0/d1 separability nearly vanishes ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$) while d1--d3 discrimination persists; this constitutes a boundary condition for the current feature set (confounded by five factors; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_confounds}).

\paragraph{Cross-strategy deployment constraint.}
Cross-strategy transfer induces a d1/d2 boundary inversion under temperature sampling.
Per-strategy z-score normalization partially corrects the inversion under logistic regression (GPT-2~XL d1v2 AUC $0.24{\to}0.56$, OLMo $0.19{\to}0.70$) but yields negligible improvement for the Random Forest ($\Delta < 0.02$\,pp); a two-stage pipeline is needed for reliable cross-strategy deployment.
In strategy-unknown settings, d1--d3 accuracy drops to 45.9\%; the pipeline recovers 11.5\,pp, though gains vary across models (GPT-2~XL $+$16.4\,pp vs.\ Pythia $+$8.0\,pp).

\paragraph{d0 inflation of headline metrics.}
Depth~0 (human-written text) is near-perfectly separable (recall $>$97\%), inflating four-class accuracy.
Cross-model transfer of 66.4\% is substantially driven by d0; d2 recall drops to 26.8\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).
We report d1--d3 balanced accuracy alongside all four-class headlines to address this inflation.

\paragraph{Domain-dependent false positive rate.}
On editorial text (WikiText-103), all classifiers achieve $\geq$98.5\% d0 accuracy, but on web-crawl data (C4, 5{,}000 passages), per-model FPR ranges from 4.7\% (OLMo) to 22.4\% (GPT-2~XL).
A pooled RF classifier evaluated on larger corpora (10{,}000 passages each) yields 34\% FPR on C4 and 17\% on FineWeb \cite{penedo2024_fineweb}; the gap reflects quality filtering in FineWeb removing feature-anomalous text that triggers false positives.
Misclassifications concentrate in template/SEO content with elevated repetition features (\texttt{rep\_3gram} $+$37\%, \texttt{rep\_4gram} $+$75\% vs.\ correctly classified d0).
Confidence thresholding ($P(\mathrm{d0}) \geq 0.15$) reduces pooled FPR from 34\%/17\% to 2.8\%/0.7\% on C4/FineWeb at minimal accuracy cost ($-$0.3\,pp); high FPR is therefore a decision-threshold problem, not a fundamental calibration defect, though the optimal threshold remains domain-dependent (Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}).

\paragraph{Adversarial robustness.}
Adversarial paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase} could disrupt the perplexity tail features that drive classification; depth estimation's robustness under such attacks is untested.

\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}
Our EDD definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically, as observed in all our configurations.
However, \citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).
Our cross-strategy transfer results provide an empirical example: training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature yields d1-vs-d2 AUC as low as 0.129 (GPT-2~XL) and 0.253 (OLMo), violating the monotonicity assumption.
In such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.
The choice of threshold $T$ is also application-dependent: at $T{=}0.80$, several cells lose one depth level relative to $T{=}0.75$.

\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}
Reference model choice affects classification accuracy by up to 11\,pp; same-family references yield optimal performance, though all configurations exceed $2.5\times$ chance.
Surprisal-based features are computed relative to Pythia-1.4B, which coincides with one of the three generators.
For the Pythia pipeline this constitutes self-model feature extraction, while OLMo and GPT-2~XL measurements are cross-model.
The self-reference configuration yields a 4--11\,pp advantage over cross-model references (Table~\ref{tab:ref_ablation}); Pythia results in Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} ($^\dagger$) should be interpreted with this caveat.
An ablation with OLMo-1B and GPT-2 XL as alternative references shows accuracy ranging from 67--79\% across three reference architectures (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), all exceeding $2.5\times$ chance; same-family reference yields optimal performance ($\Delta{\leq}$11\,pp).
The choice of reference model affects feature values; a different reference model may shift absolute feature magnitudes and potentially alter discriminability at depth boundaries.
Reference-free surface features alone achieve 53.7\% (partial signal in lexical statistics) but trail the full pipeline by 25pp; surprisal-based features are therefore essential.
Simple multi-reference ensembling does not outperform the best single reference (73.7\% vs.\ 78.6\%).

\paragraph{Single LoRA instance.}
Cross-seed replication covers 3 of 9 cells (Pythia, OLMo, GPT-2~XL nucleus); seed=43 yields $+$0.1 to $+$3.2\,pp higher accuracy, with 2/3 deltas statistically significant (non-overlapping CIs).
Feature rankings and depth ordering are consistent across seeds, but single-seed absolute accuracy carries ${\sim}$1--3\,pp uncertainty; cross-cell comparisons should be interpreted cautiously.

\paragraph{Additional caveats.}
Depth signal scales with passage length (68.4\% at 128 tokens, 77.8\% at 512; Appendix~\ref{app:length_ablation}), saturating near 500 tokens.
Prompted generation was validated on only 1 of 9 cells (GPT-2~XL nucleus); generalization to other model--strategy configurations under prompted conditions is not established.
Detection features degrade under domain shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}, and curated synthetic data may not trigger collapse \cite{falahati2026_curated}, attenuating the fingerprints we exploit.

\section*{Ethics Statement}

This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
This research used AI coding assistants for experiment implementation and writing drafts.
All scientific decisions, experimental design, and result interpretation were conducted by the authors.

1	\section{The Depth Degradation Atlas}
2	\label{sec:atlas}
3	
4	We present the Depth Degradation Atlas: a systematic empirical map of how statistical fingerprints evolve across recursive generation depths, models, and decoding strategies.
5	The atlas spans $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells evaluated at depths $d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, with depth extensions to $d{=}5$ for cross-model EDD validation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
6	
7	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
8	\subsection{In-Distribution Performance}
9	\label{sec:atlas:id}
10	
11	Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} reports four-class Random Forest accuracy (5-fold CV, 200 trees) across all nine cells.
12	Accuracy ranges from 68.9\% (Pythia, top-$k$) to 85.9\% (GPT-2~XL, temperature) four-class (d1--d3 balanced: 58.9--81.5\%), all exceeding the 25\%/33\% chance baselines.
13	Two axis effects emerge.
14	GPT-2~XL achieves the highest accuracy under every strategy (75.8--85.9\%), followed by OLMo (74.4--82.3\%) and Pythia (68.9--78.7\%).
15	Top-$k$ sampling yields the lowest accuracy in every model.
16	The mean within-model strategy gap is 9.3~pp, comparable to the 7.2~pp mean within-strategy model gap; decoding strategy and model family contribute roughly equally to performance variance.
17	
18	\begin{table}[t]
19	\centering
20	\small
21	\caption{Four-class RF accuracy (\%) with bootstrap 95\% CI (${\pm}$half-width; $B{=}1{,}000$). RF with 200 trees, evaluated via 5-fold stratified CV (seed=42). Parenthesized: d1--d3 balanced accuracy from the same 4-class RF (chance = 25\% / 33\%). Depth-0 recall exceeds 97\% in all cells. Within-distribution ordinal quality: MAE\,=\,0.23, QWK\,=\,0.89 (QWK$_{\text{d1--d3}}$\,=\,0.74); 98.2\% of errors fall on adjacent depths ($|\Delta| \leq 1$). $^\dagger$Self-reference scoring (Pythia-1.4B is both generator and reference model); 4--11\,pp advantage over cross-model references (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}).}
22	\label{tab:main_matrix}
23	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
24	\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
25	\toprule
26	& Nucleus & Temp.\ $\tau{=}0.9$ & Top-$k$ \\
27	\midrule
28	Pythia-1.4B$^\dagger$  & 78.7{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(71.8) & 76.8{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(69.3) & 68.9{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(58.9) \\
29	OLMo-1B     & 78.9{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(72.7) & 82.3{\scriptsize$\pm$0.5}\,(76.6) & 74.4{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(66.2) \\
30	GPT-2~XL    & \textbf{84.3}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.5}\,(79.6) & \textbf{85.9}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.4}\,(81.5) & \textbf{75.8}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(68.1) \\
31	\bottomrule
32	\end{tabular}}
33	\end{table}
34	
35	\paragraph{Per-class recall.}
36	Depth-0 recall exceeds 97\% in all 9 cells.
37	Among generated depths, d2 consistently yields the lowest recall (44--73\%), followed by d3 (61--80\%) and d1 (72--91\%).
38	The d2 trough reflects its position at the center of the depth gradient, where features overlap with both d1 and d3, consistent with d2-vs-d3 as the EDD bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
39	Full per-class recall appears in Appendix~\ref{app:per_class}.
40	
41	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
42	\subsection{Feature Consistency Across the Grid}
43	\label{sec:atlas:features}
44	
45	Despite the 17.1~pp accuracy spread across cells, the perplexity tail statistics family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance (\texttt{var\_surprisal}) dominate depth discrimination in every setting.
46	Within this family, \texttt{p90\_ppl} ranks top-2 by Gini importance in all 9 cells and \texttt{var\_surprisal} in 8/9 under SHAP (7/9 Gini; Appendix~\ref{app:permutation}), though individual rankings should be interpreted cautiously given high multicollinearity (VIF${>}$10 for 14--16/19 features).\footnote{The group-level dominance of perplexity tail statistics is robust across importance measures (Gini, SHAP, permutation; Kendall's $W{=}0.90$, $p{<}0.005$).}
47	Table~\ref{tab:feature_importance} shows the full per-cell ranking.
48	
49	Cross-model feature-rank Spearman correlation averages $\bar{\rho} = 0.868$ (range $[0.619, 0.954]$): models agree on which features carry depth information even when they differ in absolute accuracy.
50	Among strategies, top-$k$ yields the highest cross-model rank correlation ($\rho = 0.811$): the deterministic vocabulary truncation imposes a more uniform feature landscape across architectures, at the cost of weaker overall signal (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).
51	
52	Feature ablation confirms this concentration: the top-5 features achieve 97.6\% of full accuracy (76.5\% vs.\ 78.4\%), with perplexity statistics alone reaching 76.6\% (vs.\ surprisal 73.2\%, other categories ${\leq}$47\%).
53	
54	The feature hierarchy shifts with depth.
55	At shallow boundaries (d1 vs.\ d2), \texttt{var\_surprisal} dominates importance; at deeper boundaries (d3 vs.\ d4, d4 vs.\ d5), tail perplexity statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) take over.
56	This transition aligns with model-collapse dynamics~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}: early recursion narrows the surprisal distribution (captured by its variance), while later steps erode the perplexity tail (captured by upper quantiles and kurtosis).
57

80	
81	\begin{figure}[t]
82	\centering
83	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_atlas_heatmap.pdf}
84	\caption{Atlas feature importance heatmap. Rows: 19 features grouped by category (\S\ref{sec:method:features}); columns: 9 model--strategy cells. Color intensity encodes RF Gini importance. The perplexity-tail and surprisal-variance blocks maintain high importance across all cells.}
85	\label{fig:atlas_heatmap}
86	\end{figure}
87	
88	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
89	\subsection{Monotonicity and Inter-Depth Distances}
90	\label{sec:atlas:monotonicity}
91	
92	Depth features exhibit strong monotonic trends: perplexity tail statistics decrease with depth (Spearman $\rho = -1.0$ across cell-level medians) while repetition features increase (Figure~\ref{fig:feature_trajectory}).
93	Inter-depth distances are non-uniform: d0-vs-d1 AUC exceeds 0.99 in all 9 cells, whereas d2-vs-d3 ranges from 0.69 to 0.89.
94	
95	% Feature trajectory figure moved to Appendix for space
96	
97	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
98	\subsection{EDD Analysis}
99	\label{sec:atlas:edd}
100	
101	We extend the benchmark to depth $d{=}5$ for all three models under nucleus sampling.
102	Each model's depth-3 LoRA checkpoint is used to finetune and generate depth-4 data, and the process repeats for depth~5; feature extraction uses the same reference model (Pythia-1.4B).
103	We train dedicated binary RF classifiers (500 trees) for each adjacent pair, as defined in Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}.
104	
105	\paragraph{AUC decay and cross-model convergence.}
106	For Pythia-1.4B (nucleus), AUC decays monotonically from $0.999$ (d0v1) to $0.683$ (d4v5); AUC-excess contraction ratios (0.80 at d1v2$\to$d2v3, 0.69 at d3v4$\to$d4v5) show convergence toward indistinguishability accelerates with depth (Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay}).
107	The d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters near $T{=}0.75$ for all three models (Pythia $0.784$, OLMo $0.765$, GPT-2~XL $0.750$), while d4-vs-d5 converges to a narrow band ($0.681$--$0.684$, range $0.003$), suggesting a model-independent depth ceiling.
108	Bootstrap testing ($H_0{:}\, \mathrm{AUC} \leq 0.75$) yields $p = 0.001$ (Pythia), $0.091$ (OLMo), $0.505$ (GPT-2~XL).
109	
110	\paragraph{EDD threshold sensitivity.}
111	Across the 9-cell benchmark (depths 0--3), all cells achieve $\mathrm{EDD}{=}3$ at $T{=}0.65$; at $T{=}0.70$, 8/9 cells; at $T{=}0.75$, 7/9; at $T{=}0.80$, 5/9.
112	Top-$k$ configurations lose $\mathrm{EDD}{=}3$ first (Pythia top-$k$ at $T{=}0.70$, OLMo top-$k$ at $T{=}0.75$); d2-vs-d3 is the consistent bottleneck.
113	
114	\begin{figure}[t]
115	\centering
116	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_auc_decay.pdf}
117	\caption{Binary pairwise AUC decay curves for three models (nucleus sampling, depths 0--5). Horizontal dashed lines mark $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80\}$. All three curves converge below 0.70 at d4-vs-d5, while d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters in the range 0.750--0.784. Shaded bands: bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
118	\label{fig:auc_decay}
119	\end{figure}
120	
121	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
122	\subsection{Strategy-Dependent Trajectories}
123	\label{sec:atlas:strategy}
124	
125	The three strategies induce qualitatively distinct degradation trajectories.
126	Temperature ($\tau{=}0.9$) yields the highest accuracy in 2/3 models (GPT-2~XL 85.9\%, OLMo 82.3\%) because uniform logit scaling accelerates convergence to an attractor~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}, amplifying the fingerprint but creating a boundary reversal risk under cross-strategy transfer (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).
127	Top-$k$ ($k{=}50$) produces the lowest accuracy (68.9--75.8\%) because hard vocabulary truncation removes depth-discriminative low-probability tokens.
128	The strategy effect (9.3\,pp range) exceeds the model effect (7.2\,pp); deployment-time knowledge of the decoding strategy matters at least as much as the generator model.

I should run at least one ablation varying the rank parameter to rule this out, which is feasible since I can reuse existing features and just retrain the LoRA layer. I also haven't tested sensitivity to generation parameters — each strategy only uses one setting. 审稿人会问为什么没有测试 Binoculars 这类当前最强的二分类检测器在序数任务上的表现，但我的分类器基线覆盖已经很全面了，零样本 LLM 基线也涵盖了表面文本特征。整个论文从摘要到讨论的叙事线条是一致的，围绕全替换链、困惑度尾部特征和跨策略瓶颈展开，最近的修复也理顺了逻辑。

不过 Discussion 第 6 段关于"积累"的论述目前还只是推测性的，需要等今天下午的实验结果出来才能用真实数据验证，如果结果与预期不符就得重写。更棘手的是第三个主张关于下游应用的实验覆盖率只有三分之一，两个关键实验都失败了，这与论文把它定位为"实际贡献"的框架不太匹配。

我应该把这个主张的强度降低，改为强调方法论贡献和负面的下游分析结果。Pythia 自引用的注释在各个文档里都标注得很一致，这块没问题。现在看一下各个主张的覆盖情况汇总。

C1 的可行性和鲁棒性覆盖率达到了 76.9%，剩下的计划项都是优先级较低的。C2 关于 Atlas 和 EDD 的核心实验已经完成，只有两个计划项没做。C3 的下游应用覆盖率最低，只有 33.3%，因为只有 pipeline 成功了，其他的应用都失败了。

还有几个遗留的问题需要处理：accum_mix50 和 accum_mix25 的注册状态需要从 failed 改为 INVALIDATED，并说明是方法论错误；XGBoost 和 LightGBM 的性能声称需要提供可追溯的实验 ID；bootstrap 置信区间的计划项还没做，如果审稿人要求的话需要补上。

现在我在检查 XGBoost 和 LightGBM 的声称。摘要里说"RF、XGBoost 和 LightGBM 的收敛性证实了判别信号来自特征设计而非分类器选择"，引言里说"在 0.4pp 以内"。我在注册表里搜索 XGBoost 和 LightGBM 的实验，但在 baseline_battery_001 里只找到了 ppl_reg、ce_mlp、coral、diveye、rf、lr 的指标，没有 XGBoost 或 LightGBM 的数据。

mlp_19feat_001 也只有 MLP 变体。看起来这个声称可能来自未注册的实验，或者我需要在完整的注册表文件里搜索一下。

## 审查报告 — 等待窗口并行任务（14B 场景预判 + 论文 story 审查）

---

## Part 1: 14B 三场景叙事分析

**已知数据**：14B nucleus (scale_002) 54.05%, EDD_{0.70}=0 (d0v1 AUC=0.643)。14B temp09/topk50 RUNNING。

### [severity: warning] 14B 场景模板引用的 7-8B QLoRA 数据需要澄清

14b_scenarios.tex 三个场景均引用 "Llama-3.1-8B 70.2%" 和 "Qwen2.5-7B 60.1%"。这两个实验确实存在且 DONE（cross_scale_llama3_8b_003, cross_scale_qwen7b_001），但：

1. **paper_framing.md 称 "Prior 7B QLoRA results were contradictory due to quantization artifacts"**，措辞上覆盖了所有 QLoRA 结果，但实际只有 Qwen7B 是 contradictory（U-shape AUC, d4v5=0.772 > d3v4=0.732）；Llama8B-Instruct 是 monotonic（EDD=4）
2. **同一 scale 的 BASE 模型 accuracy 大幅低于 Instruct**: Llama-3.1-8B BASE 仅 59.9% (EDD=2) vs Instruct 70.2% (EDD=4)。Introduction L30 "7--14B (54--70%)" 中 70% 来自 instruct QLoRA，54% 来自不同模型的 FP16 clean run，把这两个不可比数据点合成一个连续范围会误导 reviewer
3. **建议**：从 introduction "54--70%" 改为按模型分开报告（如 "Qwen2.5-7B 60.1%, Llama-3.1-8B 70.2% (QLoRA), Qwen2.5-14B 54.1% (FP16)"），或仅保留同系列比较（Qwen 7B→14B: 60.1→54.1%）

### 场景评估

**Scenario A** (temp09 和 topk50 均 >50%):
- §5.4: "depth signal persists across all three strategies at 14B, confirming strategy ranking from 1-1.5B atlas"
- Abstract: 报告 14B 三策略范围
- 分数影响: 最强。直接解决 Dream M3 "14B too narrow"。建议: 焦点放 d1-d3 balanced accuracy 而非四类 accuracy（因为 d0v1 AUC=0.643 已知 EDD=0）
- **注意**: 即使三策略都 >50%，如果 strategy ranking 与 1-1.5B 不同（如 temp09 不再最优），需要在 §5.4 解释而非回避

**Scenario B** (一个 >50%, 一个~chance — 最可能场景):
- 预判根据: 1-1.5B 时 topk 始终最弱（68.9-75.8%），attenuation 最大
- §5.4: "Scale amplifies strategy-dependent attenuation"，与 atlas 一致
- Abstract: "54-X% under nucleus/temperature, top-k at chance at 14B"
- 分数影响: 中等。叙事连贯但增加 caveats

**Scenario C** (均~chance):
- §5.4: boundary condition framing — "only nucleus retains signal at 14B (54%)"
- Abstract: 仅提 nucleus
- 分数影响: 最弱但最诚实。可以转化为 "feature set limitation discovery"

**通用建议** (三场景均适用):
1. 14B EDD_{0.70}=0 是 d0/d1 separability 崩溃造成的，但 d1v2=0.713, d2v3=0.728 均 >0.70 — 真正有意义的发现是 "d0/d1 boundary vanishes but d1-d3 ordinal structure persists at 14B"。这应该成为叙事焦点
2. 模板中 "confounded by quantization" 仅修饰 14B 结果——但 14B 用的是 FP16 (无量化)；confound list 应更新
3. 删除 "cross-model chains (84.75%)" — 此数字来源不明，需要验证（registry 中 cross-model LOO 均值 66.4%）

---

## Part 2: Paper Story 完整性审查

### 1. Claim 强度

**[severity: warning] Introduction L30 "7--14B (54--70%)" 跨模型/跨量化范围误导**
详见 Part 1。70.2% = Llama-8B-Instruct QLoRA; 54% = Qwen-14B FP16。不同模型+不同精度+不同 tokenizer 合并为单一范围，reviewer 会质疑 scale attenuation 是模型差异还是规模效应。同系列数据: Qwen 7B→14B 仅 -6pp (60.1→54.1%)，而非暗示的 -16pp。

**[severity: warning] Introduction L17 "instruction-tuned variants" (plural) 过度泛化**
仅测试 2 个 instruct 模型: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (70.2%, monotonic, EDD=4) 和 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (47.4%, near chance)。两者结论相反——Llama 表现好，Qwen 接近 chance。"Instruction tuning acts as a regularizer" 的 framing 仅对 Llama 成立。且 Qwen-1.5B-Instruct pairwise AUC: d2v3=0.664 > d1v2=0.620，并非严格单调递减。建议: 措辞改为 "the sole instruction-tuned model tested at 8B scale (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) exhibits..."，或移除泛化。

**[severity: info] d4v5 收敛带可更强表述**
atlas.tex L107 "suggesting a model-independent depth ceiling" — 0.003 range 跨 3 个架构是非常强的收敛证据。但限定: 仅 nucleus、仅 1-1.5B。建议: "architecture-independent depth ceiling within the 1-1.5B nucleus setting"。

**[severity: info] 分类器收敛 claim 有实验支撑**
XGBoost/LightGBM 数据来自 xgboost_lgbm_baseline_001 和 xgboost_lgbm_3cell_001，3 个 cells 上最大 delta=0.2pp，在 claimed "0.4pp" 之内。但仅覆盖 3/9 cells — Abstract 和 Introduction 未限定此范围。低风险但可能被追问。

### 2. Ablation 盲区

**[severity: warning] LoRA hyperparameter sensitivity 缺失**
所有实验用 r=16, alpha=32, lr=2e-4。Cross-seed replication 覆盖 3/9 cells (delta 0.1-3.2pp)。审稿人可能问: "Is depth signal an artifact of a specific LoRA configuration?" Limitations 已提及（L49-51）但无消融。建议: 至少 1 个 cell 做 r={8,16,32} 消融。LoRA training 单次 ~1.5h，3 个 rank × 1 cell = ~5 GPU-h。

**[severity: info] 生成参数 (p=0.95, τ=0.9, k=50) 未做敏感性分析。标准 benchmark 做法，低风险。**

### 3. Baseline 覆盖

**[severity: warning] Binoculars / Fast-DetectGPT 未作为 ordinal baseline 测试**
plan_018 仍为 "planned"。论文引用这两个方法为相关工作，claim "binary detectors fall far below our pipeline (30-35%)"，但实际 ordinal calibration 仅测试了 DetectGPT 和 Min-K%。Binoculars 是 binary detection SOTA (Hans, ICML 2024)，未测试是明显遗漏。审稿人会问: "Binoculars achieves high binary accuracy; did you test whether its continuous scores correlate with ordinal depth?" 建议: 即使结果 negative，补测 Binoculars ordinal calibration（推理仅需 <1 GPU-h on existing data）。

### 4. 叙事一致性

**[severity: info] 主线一致性 OK**。Abstract→Introduction→Atlas→Discussion→Limitations 的全替换链→perplexity tail→EDD→cross-strategy bottleneck 叙事通畅。D044/D047 修复后自相矛盾点已清除。

**[severity: warning] Discussion accumulation 段落目前为纯预测**
L8-11: "depth signal should attenuate because each generation retains human-originated distributional properties"。accum_v3 RUNNING on westd-48862 (ETA ~14:30 UTC)。结果出来后需要用实际数据替换预测语言。如果 signal 不衰减或反而增强，Discussion 需要大幅改写。建议: 在 accum_v3 结果确认前不 finalize Discussion §6。

**[severity: warning] Claim 3 实验覆盖仅 33.3%**
Coverage matrix: Claim 3 only 1/3 plan entries done (cross-strategy pipeline +11.5pp)。downstream_curation_poc_001 = negative, downstream_benchmark_001 = failed。paper_framing.md 将 Claim 3 定位为 "practical contribution"，但 downstream 实际效果全部 negative/failed。建议: Claim 3 强度从 "practical contribution" 降为 "methodological contribution (two-stage pipeline) + negative downstream finding (data efficiency, not accuracy gain)"。

### 5. 覆盖度总结

| Claim | 覆盖率 | 评估 |
|-------|--------|------|
| C1 (可行性+鲁棒性) | 76.9% (20/26) | 充分。6 planned 中 4 为 P1/P2 |

### 6. 遗留事项

1. **accum_mix50/accum_mix25** registry 状态仍为 "failed"，应改为 "INVALIDATED" + methodology note (feature-space mixing 而非 training-level accumulation)。此前已报告，未确认是否执行

78	def load_cell_texts(cell_dir, max_samples=0):

97	def _skewness(x):
98	    """Sample skewness without scipy."""
99	    if len(x) < 3:
100	        return 0.0
101	    m = np.mean(x)
102	    s = np.std(x, ddof=0)
103	    if s < 1e-12:
104	        return 0.0
105	    return float(np.mean(((x - m) / s) ** 3))

108	# ── Binoculars scorer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
109	
110	class BinocularsScorer:
111	    """Compute Binoculars features using observer and performer LMs.
112	
113	    Core formula (Hans et al. 2024):
114	        score = PPL(x; performer) / H(observer, performer)
115	    where PPL is standard per-token CE against actual tokens, and H is the
116	    cross-entropy between the observer's softmax distribution and the
117	    performer's logits at each position.
118	    """
119	
120	    def __init__(self, observer_name, performer_name, device,
121	                 max_length=MAX_LENGTH):
122	        self.device = device
123	        self.max_length = max_length
124	
125	        print(f"Loading tokenizer: {observer_name}")
126	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(observer_name)
127	        if self.tokenizer.pad_token is None:
128	            self.tokenizer.pad_token = self.tokenizer.eos_token
129	        self.pad_token_id = self.tokenizer.pad_token_id
130	
131	        print(f"Loading observer:  {observer_name}")
132	        self.observer = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
133	            observer_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16,
134	        ).to(device).eval()
135	
136	        print(f"Loading performer: {performer_name}")
137	        self.performer = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
138	            performer_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16,
139	        ).to(device).eval()
140	
141	        self.ce_loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")
142	        self.softmax_fn = nn.Softmax(dim=-1)
143	
144	    @torch.no_grad()
145	    def compute_features(self, texts, batch_size=8):
146	        """Compute per-sample Binoculars-derived features.
147	
148	        For each text, runs both models and extracts:
149	          - Standard Binoculars score (ppl_mean / xppl_mean)
150	          - Token-level statistics of PPL and cross-entropy
151	
152	        Returns dict mapping feature name -> np.array of shape (n_samples,).
153	        """
154	        feats = {k: [] for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES}
155	
156	        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(texts), batch_size),
157	                      desc="  Binoculars scoring"):
158	            batch = texts[i:i + batch_size]
159	            enc = self.tokenizer(
160	                batch,
161	                max_length=self.max_length,
162	                truncation=True,
163	                padding=True,
164	                return_tensors="pt",
165	                return_attention_mask=True,
166	            ).to(self.device)
167	
168	            obs_logits = self.observer(**enc).logits
169	            perf_logits = self.performer(**enc).logits
170	
171	            # ── Per-token perplexity: performer predicts next token ──
172	            shifted_perf = perf_logits[:, :-1, :].contiguous().float()
173	            shifted_labels = enc.input_ids[:, 1:].contiguous()
174	            shifted_mask = enc.attention_mask[:, 1:].contiguous().bool()
175	            ppl_tok = self.ce_loss_fn(
176	                shifted_perf.transpose(1, 2), shifted_labels,
177	            )  # (B, T-1)
178	
179	            # ── Per-token cross-entropy: observer dist vs performer logits ──
180	            # No shift — matches original Binoculars implementation.
181	            B, T, V = obs_logits.shape
182	            obs_probs = self.softmax_fn(obs_logits.float()).reshape(-1, V)
183	            perf_flat = perf_logits.float().reshape(-1, V)
184	            xppl_tok = self.ce_loss_fn(perf_flat, obs_probs).reshape(B, T)
185	            full_mask = (enc.input_ids != self.pad_token_id)
186	
187	            # ── Extract per-sample statistics ──
188	            for b in range(len(batch)):
189	                pv = ppl_tok[b][shifted_mask[b]].cpu().numpy()
190	                xv = xppl_tok[b][full_mask[b]].cpu().numpy()
191	
192	                if len(pv) < 2 or len(xv) < 2:
193	                    for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES:
194	                        feats[k].append(0.0)
195	                    continue
196	
197	                pm = float(np.mean(pv))
198	                xm = float(np.mean(xv))
199	                p_med = float(np.median(pv))
200	                x_med = float(np.median(xv))
201	
202	                feats["bino_score"].append(
203	                    pm / xm if xm > 1e-8 else 0.0)
204	                feats["ppl_mean"].append(pm)
205	                feats["ppl_var"].append(float(np.var(pv)))
206	                feats["ppl_median"].append(p_med)
207	                feats["ppl_p10"].append(float(np.percentile(pv, 10)))
208	                feats["ppl_p90"].append(float(np.percentile(pv, 90)))
209	                feats["ppl_skew"].append(_skewness(pv))
210	                feats["xppl_mean"].append(xm)
211	                feats["xppl_var"].append(float(np.var(xv)))
212	                feats["xppl_median"].append(x_med)
213	                feats["bino_score_median"].append(
214	                    p_med / x_med if x_med > 1e-8 else 0.0)
215	
216	            del obs_logits, perf_logits, shifted_perf, obs_probs
217	            del perf_flat, ppl_tok, xppl_tok
218	            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
219	
220	        return {k: np.array(v, dtype=np.float64) for k, v in feats.items()}

223	# ── Calibration methods (matching detectgpt/mink baselines) ────────────────

225	def calibrate_equal_width(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
226	    """Equal-width binning. Tries both score directions, picks better."""
227	    lo, hi = s_tr.min(), s_tr.max()
228	    if hi - lo < 1e-12:
229	        return np.zeros(len(s_te), dtype=int)
230	    width = (hi - lo + 1e-8) / 4
231	
232	    best_preds, best_acc = None, -1
233	    for ascending in [True, False]:
234	        if ascending:
235	            p_tr = np.clip(((s_tr - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
236	            p_te = np.clip(((s_te - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
237	        else:
238	            p_tr = np.clip(3 - ((s_tr - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
239	            p_te = np.clip(3 - ((s_te - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
240	        acc = accuracy_score(y_tr, p_tr)
241	        if acc > best_acc:
242	            best_acc, best_preds = acc, p_te
243	    return best_preds
244

246	class _CoralOrdinal(nn.Module):
247	    """CORAL ordinal regression: shared linear + per-boundary biases."""
248	
249	    def __init__(self, n_classes=4):
250	        super().__init__()
251	        self.linear = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
252	        self.biases = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(n_classes - 1))
253	
254	    def forward(self, x):
255	        return self.linear(x) + self.biases  # (N, K-1)
256	
257	
258	def calibrate_coral(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
259	    """CORAL ordinal regression (1-D score -> 4-class)."""
260	    X_tr = torch.tensor(s_tr, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
261	    X_te = torch.tensor(s_te, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
262	
263	    y_ord = torch.zeros(len(y_tr), 3)
264	    for j in range(3):
265	        y_ord[:, j] = (torch.tensor(y_tr) > j).float()
266	
267	    model = _CoralOrdinal()
268	    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
269	    crit = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
270	
271	    model.train()
272	    for _ in range(300):
273	        loss = crit(model(X_tr), y_ord)
274	        opt.zero_grad()
275	        loss.backward()
276	        opt.step()
277	
278	    model.eval()
279	    with torch.no_grad():
280	        probs = torch.sigmoid(model(X_te))
281	        preds = (probs > 0.5).sum(dim=1).numpy().astype(int)
282	    return np.clip(preds, 0, 3)

285	def calibrate_threshold(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
286	    """ROC-optimal thresholds for each depth boundary.
287	
288	    Tries both score directions to handle unknown monotonicity.
289	    """
290	    best_preds_test, best_acc = None, -1
291	
292	    for flip in [False, True]:
293	        st = -s_tr if flip else s_tr.copy()
294	        ste = -s_te if flip else s_te.copy()
295	
296	        thresholds = []
297	        for boundary in range(1, 4):
298	            y_bin = (y_tr >= boundary).astype(int)
299	            if len(np.unique(y_bin)) < 2:
300	                thresholds.append(np.median(st))
301	                continue
302	            fpr, tpr, thresh = roc_curve(y_bin, st)
303	            best_idx = np.argmax(tpr - fpr)
304	            thresholds.append(thresh[best_idx])
305	
306	        thresholds = sorted(thresholds)
307	        p_tr = np.zeros(len(st), dtype=int)
308	        for t in thresholds:
309	            p_tr += (st >= t).astype(int)
310	        p_tr = np.clip(p_tr, 0, 3)
311	        acc = accuracy_score(y_tr, p_tr)
312	
313	        if acc > best_acc:
314	            best_acc = acc
315	            p_te = np.zeros(len(ste), dtype=int)
316	            for t in thresholds:
317	                p_te += (ste >= t).astype(int)
318	            best_preds_test = np.clip(p_te, 0, 3)
319	
320	    return best_preds_test

323	# ── RF classifiers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
324	
325	def rf_single_feature(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
326	    """RF with Binoculars score as sole feature."""
327	    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
328	        n_estimators=RF_N_ESTIMATORS, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
329	    )
330	    clf.fit(s_tr.reshape(-1, 1), y_tr)

333	
334	def rf_multi_feature(X_tr, y_tr, X_te):
335	    """RF with 11 Binoculars-derived features."""
336	    scaler = StandardScaler()
337	    Xtr = np.nan_to_num(scaler.fit_transform(X_tr), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0,
338	                        neginf=0.0)
339	    Xte = np.nan_to_num(scaler.transform(X_te), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0,

341	    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
342	        n_estimators=RF_N_ESTIMATORS, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
343	    )
344	    clf.fit(Xtr, y_tr)
345	    return clf.predict(Xte)

348	# ── 5-fold CV evaluation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
349	
350	def evaluate_cell(features, labels):
351	    """Run 5-fold StratifiedKFold CV for all five methods.
352	
353	    Args:
354	        features: dict of feature arrays (each shape (n,))
355	        labels: int array of depth labels
356	
357	    Returns:
358	        dict of method -> {4class_acc, 4class_acc_std,
359	                           d1d3_bal_acc, d1d3_bal_acc_std}
360	    """
361	    scores = features["bino_score"]
362	    X_multi = np.column_stack([features[k] for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES])
363	
364	    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=N_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
365	
366	    METHODS = [
367	        ("equal_width", True),
368	        ("coral",       True),
369	        ("threshold",   True),
370	        ("RF_single",   True),
371	        ("RF_multi",    False),
372	    ]
373	
374	    results = {}
375	    for method_name, uses_score_only in METHODS:
376	        fold_acc4, fold_bal = [], []
377	
378	        for train_idx, test_idx in skf.split(scores, labels):
379	            s_tr = scores[train_idx]
380	            s_te = scores[test_idx]
381	            y_tr = labels[train_idx]
382	            y_te = labels[test_idx]
383	
384	            if method_name == "equal_width":
385	                preds = calibrate_equal_width(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
386	            elif method_name == "coral":

388	            elif method_name == "threshold":

390	            elif method_name == "RF_single":
391	                preds = rf_single_feature(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
392	            elif method_name == "RF_multi":
393	                preds = rf_multi_feature(

396	            fold_acc4.append(accuracy_score(y_te, preds))

398	            mask = y_te >= 1

402	            else:
403	                fold_bal.append(0.0)
404	
405	        results[method_name] = {
406	            "4class_acc":       round(float(np.mean(fold_acc4)), 4),
407	            "4class_acc_std":   round(float(np.std(fold_acc4)), 4),
408	            "d1d3_bal_acc":     round(float(np.mean(fold_bal)), 4),
409	            "d1d3_bal_acc_std": round(float(np.std(fold_bal)), 4),
410	        }
411	
412	    return results

"""Binoculars ordinal depth baseline (Hans et al., ICML 2024).

Computes Binoculars scores using an observer model (pythia-1.4b) and a
performer model (pythia-410m), then evaluates ordinal depth classification
(d0-d3) via five methods: equal-width binning, CORAL ordinal regression,
threshold-based ROC optimization, single-feature RF, and multi-feature RF.

Input:
    --data_dir pointing to root with cell subdirectories, each containing
    depth_0.jsonl .. depth_3.jsonl.  Each JSONL record has a "text" field.

Output:
    JSON with per-cell and 9-cell-average metrics:
      {4class_acc, 4class_acc_std, d1d3_bal_acc, d1d3_bal_acc_std}
    Also saves per-cell .npz files with raw features and labels.

Dependencies: torch, transformers, scikit-learn, numpy, tqdm
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import time
import warnings
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, balanced_accuracy_score, roc_curve
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from tqdm import tqdm
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

os.environ.setdefault("HF_ENDPOINT", "https://hf-mirror.com")

SEED = 42
N_FOLDS = 5
MAX_LENGTH = 512
RF_N_ESTIMATORS = 200

CELL_SUBDIRS = {
    "pythia_nucleus": ".",
    "pythia_temp09":  "pythia_temp09",
    "pythia_topk50":  "pythia_topk50",
    "olmo_nucleus":   "olmo",
    "olmo_temp09":    "olmo_temp09",
    "olmo_topk50":    "olmo_topk50",
    "gpt2xl_nucleus": "gpt2xl",
    "gpt2xl_temp09":  "gpt2xl_temp09",
    "gpt2xl_topk50":  "gpt2xl_topk50",
}

MULTI_FEAT_NAMES = [
    "bino_score",
    "ppl_mean", "ppl_var", "ppl_median", "ppl_p10", "ppl_p90", "ppl_skew",
    "xppl_mean", "xppl_var", "xppl_median",
    "bino_score_median",
]


# ── Utilities ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def set_seed(seed=SEED):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def load_cell_texts(cell_dir, max_samples=0):
    """Load depth_0..3.jsonl from cell_dir. Returns (texts, labels)."""
    texts, labels = [], []
    for d in range(4):
        fpath = cell_dir / f"depth_{d}.jsonl"
        if not fpath.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing {fpath}")
        lines = [ln for ln in fpath.read_text().strip().split("\n") if ln.strip()]
        if 0 < max_samples < len(lines):
            rng = np.random.RandomState(SEED + d)
            idx = rng.choice(len(lines), max_samples, replace=False)
            lines = [lines[i] for i in sorted(idx)]
        for line in lines:
            rec = json.loads(line)
            texts.append(rec["text"])
            labels.append(d)
    return texts, np.array(labels, dtype=np.int64)


def _skewness(x):
    """Sample skewness without scipy."""
    if len(x) < 3:
        return 0.0
    m = np.mean(x)
    s = np.std(x, ddof=0)
    if s < 1e-12:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.mean(((x - m) / s) ** 3))


# ── Binoculars scorer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class BinocularsScorer:
    """Compute Binoculars features using observer and performer LMs.

    Core formula (Hans et al. 2024):
        score = PPL(x; performer) / H(observer, performer)
    where PPL is standard per-token CE against actual tokens, and H is the
    cross-entropy between the observer's softmax distribution and the
    performer's logits at each position.
    """

    def __init__(self, observer_name, performer_name, device,
                 max_length=MAX_LENGTH):
        self.device = device
        self.max_length = max_length

        print(f"Loading tokenizer: {observer_name}")
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(observer_name)
        if self.tokenizer.pad_token is None:
            self.tokenizer.pad_token = self.tokenizer.eos_token
        self.pad_token_id = self.tokenizer.pad_token_id

        print(f"Loading observer:  {observer_name}")
        self.observer = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            observer_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16,
        ).to(device).eval()

        print(f"Loading performer: {performer_name}")
        self.performer = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            performer_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16,
        ).to(device).eval()

        self.ce_loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")
        self.softmax_fn = nn.Softmax(dim=-1)

    @torch.no_grad()
    def compute_features(self, texts, batch_size=8):
        """Compute per-sample Binoculars-derived features.

        For each text, runs both models and extracts:
          - Standard Binoculars score (ppl_mean / xppl_mean)
          - Token-level statistics of PPL and cross-entropy

        Returns dict mapping feature name -> np.array of shape (n_samples,).
        """
        feats = {k: [] for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES}

        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(texts), batch_size),
                      desc="  Binoculars scoring"):
            batch = texts[i:i + batch_size]
            enc = self.tokenizer(
                batch,
                max_length=self.max_length,
                truncation=True,
                padding=True,
                return_tensors="pt",
                return_attention_mask=True,
            ).to(self.device)

            obs_logits = self.observer(**enc).logits
            perf_logits = self.performer(**enc).logits

            # ── Per-token perplexity: performer predicts next token ──
            shifted_perf = perf_logits[:, :-1, :].contiguous().float()
            shifted_labels = enc.input_ids[:, 1:].contiguous()
            shifted_mask = enc.attention_mask[:, 1:].contiguous().bool()
            ppl_tok = self.ce_loss_fn(
                shifted_perf.transpose(1, 2), shifted_labels,
            )  # (B, T-1)

            # ── Per-token cross-entropy: observer dist vs performer logits ──
            # No shift — matches original Binoculars implementation.
            B, T, V = obs_logits.shape
            obs_probs = self.softmax_fn(obs_logits.float()).reshape(-1, V)
            perf_flat = perf_logits.float().reshape(-1, V)
            xppl_tok = self.ce_loss_fn(perf_flat, obs_probs).reshape(B, T)
            full_mask = (enc.input_ids != self.pad_token_id)

            # ── Extract per-sample statistics ──
            for b in range(len(batch)):
                pv = ppl_tok[b][shifted_mask[b]].cpu().numpy()
                xv = xppl_tok[b][full_mask[b]].cpu().numpy()

                if len(pv) < 2 or len(xv) < 2:
                    for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES:
                        feats[k].append(0.0)
                    continue

                pm = float(np.mean(pv))
                xm = float(np.mean(xv))
                p_med = float(np.median(pv))
                x_med = float(np.median(xv))

                feats["bino_score"].append(
                    pm / xm if xm > 1e-8 else 0.0)
                feats["ppl_mean"].append(pm)
                feats["ppl_var"].append(float(np.var(pv)))
                feats["ppl_median"].append(p_med)
                feats["ppl_p10"].append(float(np.percentile(pv, 10)))
                feats["ppl_p90"].append(float(np.percentile(pv, 90)))
                feats["ppl_skew"].append(_skewness(pv))
                feats["xppl_mean"].append(xm)
                feats["xppl_var"].append(float(np.var(xv)))
                feats["xppl_median"].append(x_med)
                feats["bino_score_median"].append(
                    p_med / x_med if x_med > 1e-8 else 0.0)

            del obs_logits, perf_logits, shifted_perf, obs_probs
            del perf_flat, ppl_tok, xppl_tok
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

        return {k: np.array(v, dtype=np.float64) for k, v in feats.items()}


# ── Calibration methods (matching detectgpt/mink baselines) ────────────────

def calibrate_equal_width(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
    """Equal-width binning. Tries both score directions, picks better."""
    lo, hi = s_tr.min(), s_tr.max()
    if hi - lo < 1e-12:
        return np.zeros(len(s_te), dtype=int)
    width = (hi - lo + 1e-8) / 4

    best_preds, best_acc = None, -1
    for ascending in [True, False]:
        if ascending:
            p_tr = np.clip(((s_tr - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
            p_te = np.clip(((s_te - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
        else:
            p_tr = np.clip(3 - ((s_tr - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
            p_te = np.clip(3 - ((s_te - lo) / width).astype(int), 0, 3)
        acc = accuracy_score(y_tr, p_tr)
        if acc > best_acc:
            best_acc, best_preds = acc, p_te
    return best_preds


class _CoralOrdinal(nn.Module):
    """CORAL ordinal regression: shared linear + per-boundary biases."""

    def __init__(self, n_classes=4):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
        self.biases = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(n_classes - 1))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.linear(x) + self.biases  # (N, K-1)


def calibrate_coral(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
    """CORAL ordinal regression (1-D score -> 4-class)."""
    X_tr = torch.tensor(s_tr, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
    X_te = torch.tensor(s_te, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)

    y_ord = torch.zeros(len(y_tr), 3)
    for j in range(3):
        y_ord[:, j] = (torch.tensor(y_tr) > j).float()

    model = _CoralOrdinal()
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    crit = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()

    model.train()
    for _ in range(300):
        loss = crit(model(X_tr), y_ord)
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()

    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        probs = torch.sigmoid(model(X_te))
        preds = (probs > 0.5).sum(dim=1).numpy().astype(int)
    return np.clip(preds, 0, 3)


def calibrate_threshold(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
    """ROC-optimal thresholds for each depth boundary.

    Tries both score directions to handle unknown monotonicity.
    """
    best_preds_test, best_acc = None, -1

    for flip in [False, True]:
        st = -s_tr if flip else s_tr.copy()
        ste = -s_te if flip else s_te.copy()

        thresholds = []
        for boundary in range(1, 4):
            y_bin = (y_tr >= boundary).astype(int)
            if len(np.unique(y_bin)) < 2:
                thresholds.append(np.median(st))
                continue
            fpr, tpr, thresh = roc_curve(y_bin, st)
            best_idx = np.argmax(tpr - fpr)
            thresholds.append(thresh[best_idx])

        thresholds = sorted(thresholds)
        p_tr = np.zeros(len(st), dtype=int)
        for t in thresholds:
            p_tr += (st >= t).astype(int)
        p_tr = np.clip(p_tr, 0, 3)
        acc = accuracy_score(y_tr, p_tr)

        if acc > best_acc:
            best_acc = acc
            p_te = np.zeros(len(ste), dtype=int)
            for t in thresholds:
                p_te += (ste >= t).astype(int)
            best_preds_test = np.clip(p_te, 0, 3)

    return best_preds_test


# ── RF classifiers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def rf_single_feature(s_tr, y_tr, s_te):
    """RF with Binoculars score as sole feature."""
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=RF_N_ESTIMATORS, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
    )
    clf.fit(s_tr.reshape(-1, 1), y_tr)
    return clf.predict(s_te.reshape(-1, 1))


def rf_multi_feature(X_tr, y_tr, X_te):
    """RF with 11 Binoculars-derived features."""
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    Xtr = np.nan_to_num(scaler.fit_transform(X_tr), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0,
                        neginf=0.0)
    Xte = np.nan_to_num(scaler.transform(X_te), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0,
                        neginf=0.0)
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=RF_N_ESTIMATORS, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
    )
    clf.fit(Xtr, y_tr)
    return clf.predict(Xte)


# ── 5-fold CV evaluation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

def evaluate_cell(features, labels):
    """Run 5-fold StratifiedKFold CV for all five methods.

    Args:
        features: dict of feature arrays (each shape (n,))
        labels: int array of depth labels

    Returns:
        dict of method -> {4class_acc, 4class_acc_std,
                           d1d3_bal_acc, d1d3_bal_acc_std}
    """
    scores = features["bino_score"]
    X_multi = np.column_stack([features[k] for k in MULTI_FEAT_NAMES])

    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=N_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)

    METHODS = [
        ("equal_width", True),
        ("coral",       True),
        ("threshold",   True),
        ("RF_single",   True),
        ("RF_multi",    False),
    ]

    results = {}
    for method_name, uses_score_only in METHODS:
        fold_acc4, fold_bal = [], []

        for train_idx, test_idx in skf.split(scores, labels):
            s_tr = scores[train_idx]
            s_te = scores[test_idx]
            y_tr = labels[train_idx]
            y_te = labels[test_idx]

            if method_name == "equal_width":
                preds = calibrate_equal_width(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
            elif method_name == "coral":
                preds = calibrate_coral(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
            elif method_name == "threshold":
                preds = calibrate_threshold(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
            elif method_name == "RF_single":
                preds = rf_single_feature(s_tr, y_tr, s_te)
            elif method_name == "RF_multi":
                preds = rf_multi_feature(
                    X_multi[train_idx], y_tr, X_multi[test_idx])

            fold_acc4.append(accuracy_score(y_te, preds))

            mask = y_te >= 1
            if mask.sum() > 0:
                fold_bal.append(
                    balanced_accuracy_score(y_te[mask], preds[mask]))
            else:
                fold_bal.append(0.0)

        results[method_name] = {
            "4class_acc":       round(float(np.mean(fold_acc4)), 4),
            "4class_acc_std":   round(float(np.std(fold_acc4)), 4),
            "d1d3_bal_acc":     round(float(np.mean(fold_bal)), 4),
            "d1d3_bal_acc_std": round(float(np.std(fold_bal)), 4),
        }

    return results


# ── Main ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Binoculars ordinal depth baseline (Hans et al. 2024)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--data_dir", type=str, required=True,
        help="Root data dir with cell subdirs containing depth_0..3.jsonl")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--observer_model", type=str, default="EleutherAI/pythia-1.4b",
        help="Observer model (larger, default: pythia-1.4b)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--performer_model", type=str, default="EleutherAI/pythia-410m",
        help="Performer model (smaller, default: pythia-410m)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output_path", type=str, required=True,
        help="Output JSON path for results")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--gpu", type=int, default=0, help="GPU device ID")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max_samples", type=int, default=0,
        help="Max samples per depth (0 = use all, >0 for debugging)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--batch_size", type=int, default=8,
        help="Batch size for model inference (default: 8)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    set_seed()
    data_root = Path(args.data_dir)
    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{args.gpu}")

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Binoculars Ordinal Depth Baseline")
    print(f"  Observer:  {args.observer_model}")
    print(f"  Performer: {args.performer_model}")
    print(f"  Device:    {device}")
    print(f"  Data root: {data_root}")
    print(f"  Max samples/depth: {args.max_samples or 'all (5000)'}")
    print(f"  Batch size: {args.batch_size}")
    print("=" * 60)

    scorer = BinocularsScorer(
        args.observer_model, args.performer_model,
        device, max_length=MAX_LENGTH,
    )

    all_results = {}
    cell_times = {}

    for cell_name, subdir in CELL_SUBDIRS.items():
        cell_dir = data_root / subdir if subdir != "." else data_root
        if not (cell_dir / "depth_0.jsonl").exists():
            print(f"\nSkipping {cell_name}: "
                  f"{cell_dir}/depth_0.jsonl not found")
            continue

        print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
        print(f"Cell: {cell_name}  ({cell_dir})")
        print(f"{'=' * 60}")

        t0 = time.time()
        texts, labels = load_cell_texts(
            cell_dir, max_samples=args.max_samples)
        print(f"  Loaded {len(texts)} samples, "
              f"depths: {np.bincount(labels).tolist()}")

        features = scorer.compute_features(texts, batch_size=args.batch_size)
        bino = features["bino_score"]
        print(f"  Binoculars score: mean={bino.mean():.4f}, "
              f"std={bino.std():.4f}, "
              f"min={bino.min():.4f}, max={bino.max():.4f}")

        out_dir = Path(args.output_path).parent
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        np.savez(
            out_dir / f"{cell_name}_bino_features.npz",
            **features, labels=labels,
        )

        cell_results = evaluate_cell(features, labels)
        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        cell_times[cell_name] = round(elapsed, 1)

        for method, m in cell_results.items():
            print(f"  {method:12s}: "
                  f"acc={m['4class_acc']:.4f}+/-{m['4class_acc_std']:.4f}  "
                  f"d1d3_bal={m['d1d3_bal_acc']:.4f}"
                  f"+/-{m['d1d3_bal_acc_std']:.4f}")

        all_results[cell_name] = cell_results

        with open(args.output_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(all_results, f, indent=2)

    # ── 9-cell average ──
    if all_results:
        avg = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
        for cell_res in all_results.values():
            for method, metrics in cell_res.items():
                for k, v in metrics.items():
                    avg[method][k].append(v)

        all_results["__9cell_average__"] = {}
        for method, ml in avg.items():
            all_results["__9cell_average__"][method] = {
                k: round(float(np.mean(v)), 4) for k, v in ml.items()
            }

        all_results["__meta__"] = {
            "observer": args.observer_model,
            "performer": args.performer_model,
            "max_samples_per_depth": args.max_samples or "all",
            "n_folds": N_FOLDS,
            "rf_n_estimators": RF_N_ESTIMATORS,
            "multi_features": MULTI_FEAT_NAMES,
            "cell_times_sec": cell_times,
            "total_time_sec": round(sum(cell_times.values()), 1),
        }

    with open(args.output_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(all_results, f, indent=2)
    print(f"\nResults saved to {args.output_path}")

    # ── Summary table ──
    print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
    print("9-Cell Average Summary")
    print(f"{'=' * 60}")
    if "__9cell_average__" in all_results:
        for method, m in all_results["__9cell_average__"].items():
            print(f"  {method:12s}: "
                  f"acc={m['4class_acc']:.4f}  "
                  f"d1d3_bal={m['d1d3_bal_acc']:.4f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The real question is whether these 11 multi-features—which extend beyond standard Binoculars by incorporating token-level statistics from the scoring process—are actually capturing meaningful signal or just adding noise.
